issues.description: The method Animal.messageOnFeed() has conflicting return types across artifacts. The problem statement UML declares messageOnFeed(): String (problem_statement.md lines 26-29). In the solution, Animal.java declares public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed(); (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 18) and a new FeedResponse class is introduced (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/FeedResponse.java line 3). Two concrete solution classes (Pig and Seal) implement messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Pig.java line 10 and solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 13), but Goat.java in the solution incorrectly overrides messageOnFeed() with a String return type (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java lines 10-11). This mismatch between the exercise description/template (expecting String) and the solution (using FeedResponse), plus the inconsistent Goat implementation, will confuse students and can cause compilation or overriding errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of Animal.messageOnFeed() consistent across all artifacts. Recommended (to match the problem statement and template): change the solution to have Animal.messageOnFeed() return String, remove the FeedResponse class (or stop using it for messageOnFeed), and update Pig and Seal to return the specified String messages (e.g., "Oink!", "Arf Arf!", "Maah!"). Alternatively, if FeedResponse is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement, UML, and template code to specify messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse and show how callers (Farm.feedAllAnimals and singFarmSong) should extract and print the message (e.g., call feedResponse.toString() or getMessage()). Also fix Goat.java so it overrides with the correct return type to match Animal's signature.
